question.problem:
A physics experiment consists of a small object moving along a straight line. The following table contains data collected on the distance traveled by the object (in inches) during the first five seconds. 

| Time $(x)$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Distance $(y)$ | $8.6$ | $13.1$ | $24.6$ | $28.1$ | $38.6$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what distance will the object cover after $6$ seconds, assuming the trend continues? 

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}11 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}113 \\ 414\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
question.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}8.6 \\ 13.1 \\ 24.6 \\ 28.1 \\ 38.6\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}11 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}113 \\ 414\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.1 \\ 7.5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the line $y=0.1+7.5x.$

Finally, to predict the distance the object will cover after $6$ seconds, we substitute $x=6$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =0.1+7.5(6) \\  & =45.1\end{aligned}
$$

So, according to the model, the object will cover a distance of $45.1$ inches in $6$ seconds.  

**Note**: Since we're extrapolating ($x=6$ is not within the range of the original set of $x$-values), our result *may* be unreliable.
